content.user_title: Build Azure Web PubSub Python Workflows
content.value_statement: Real-time WebSocket apps need clear service-side and client-side patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Azure Web PubSub Python guidance.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation steps for Azure Web PubSub service and client SDK packages.
Demonstrates service client authentication with connection strings and Entra ID.
Explains client access token generation for users, roles, and groups.
Covers sending messages to all clients, users, groups, and connections.
Summarizes group, connection, permission, async, and client SDK operations.
limitations: Does not provision Azure Web PubSub resources or configure Azure subscriptions.
Does not validate live credentials, hub names, endpoints, or access policies.
Uses placeholder values that users must replace before implementation.
Does not replace production security testing or Azure architecture review.

use_cases.title: Create a WebSocket Backend
use_cases.description: Plan Python service code that authenticates with Azure Web PubSub and sends messages to connected clients.

use_cases.title: Design Group Messaging
use_cases.description: Map user and connection membership into Azure Web PubSub groups for targeted real-time updates.

use_cases.title: Review Messaging Operations
use_cases.description: Check which SDK operations support token generation, broadcasting, permissions, and connection management.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Service Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to initialize an Azure Web PubSub Service client in Python using this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Client Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an access token plan for Azure Web PubSub users with limited roles and group access.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Targeted Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python messaging flow that sends updates to all clients, one user, one group, and one connection.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Web PubSub Python design for token lifetime, group permissions, reconnection handling, and credential safety.

output_examples.input: Create a server-side Azure Web PubSub setup outline.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan covering package installation, credential selection, hub configuration, and service client initialization.

output_examples.input: Explain how to send messages to groups and users.
output_examples.output: A plain-language comparison of broadcast, user, group, and connection messaging with recommended use cases.
A checklist covering scoped roles, short-lived tokens, group membership, permission revocation, and graceful connection closure.

best_practices: Use short-lived access tokens with the smallest roles needed for each client.
Store connection strings in approved secret stores or environment variables.
Separate broadcast, user, group, and connection messaging decisions clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real Azure access keys in source files or prompts.
Do not grant broad send or group permissions to every client token.
Do not skip reconnection and graceful close behavior in client applications.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Python workflows for Azure Web PubSub service clients and WebSocket clients.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK guidance, but users must create and configure Azure resources separately.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows connection string and Entra ID patterns for service client authentication.

faq.question: Can it generate WebSocket access tokens?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers token generation with user IDs, roles, and group membership.

faq.question: Does it support async Python examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes an async service client example using Azure identity credentials.

faq.question: Is it safe to paste production secrets?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders in prompts and keep production secrets in approved secret management systems.
